The following sketch represents the electroplating of an Iron cup with Nickel metal. Study the diagram and answer the following questions. (Sketch: an iron cup connected as cathode and a nickel anode dipping in an electrolyte.)
(a) During electroplating the iron cup is placed at the cathode. Why?
questions.solution: The article to be electroplated is always made the cathode so that the metal ions (Ni2+) are reduced (gain electrons) and deposited as a layer on it.

marking_points.point: Article to be plated is the cathode, where metal (Ni2+) ions are reduced/deposited on it

answer_items.prompt: Ion that must be present in the electrolyte

questions.solution: Ni2+ (nickel ions); the anion depends on the electrolyte taken.

questions.question:
The following sketch represents the electroplating of an Iron cup with Nickel metal. Study the diagram and answer the following questions. (Sketch: an iron cup connected as cathode and a nickel anode dipping in an electrolyte.)
(c) State one condition that is necessary to ensure that the deposit is smooth, firm and even.
questions.solution: Passing a low current for a long time (a low current density) ensures a smooth, firm and even deposit. (Also acceptable: low temperature/ proper cleaning of article.)

marking_points.point: Low current for a long time / low current density

questions.question:
The following sketch represents the electroplating of an Iron cup with Nickel metal. Study the diagram and answer the following questions. (Sketch: an iron cup connected as cathode and a nickel anode dipping in an electrolyte.)

The following sketch represents the electroplating of an Iron cup with Nickel metal. Study the diagram and answer the following questions. (Sketch: an iron cup connected as cathode and a nickel anode dipping in an electrolyte.)
(e) What change would you observe at the anode?
questions.solution: The nickel anode dissolves (Ni -> Ni2+ + 2e-), so the anode becomes thinner while the iron cup becomes thicker (gets plated).

marking_points.point: Anode dissolves / becomes thinner (Ni -> Ni2+ + 2e-)

questions.question:
Ammonia burns in oxygen as shown below.
4NH3 + 3O2 -> 2N2 + 6H2O
If 240 cc of ammonia is burnt in 300 cc of oxygen, find out the composition of the resultant gaseous mixture at room temperature.
questions.solution: 4 cc NH3 reacts with 3 cc O2, so 240 cc NH3 needs 240 x 3/4 = 180 cc O2. Unused O2 = 300 - 180 = 120 cc. N2 formed = 240 x 2/4 = 120 cc. Water formed condenses at room temperature (liquid) and is not counted. Resultant mixture: 120 cc N2 + 120 cc O2 (total 240 cc). (The printed answer is garbled: it gives only '120 cc'.)

marking_points.point: Volume ratio: 4NH3 needs 3O2, so 180 cc O2 used
Unused O2 = 120 cc; N2 formed = 120 cc
Steam condenses; mixture = 120 cc N2 + 120 cc O2

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Property of H2SO4 in HCl preparation
questions.question:
Hydrogen chloride gas is prepared in the laboratory by the action of concentrated sulphuric acid on sodium chloride.
(c) What is property of sulphuric acid that makes it a suitable reagent for the reaction.
questions.solution: Sulphuric acid is non-volatile (high boiling point), so it displaces the more volatile HCl from the chloride. The printed key also says 'oxidising agent', which is not the relevant property here (H2SO4 does not oxidise HCl in this preparation); the credited answer is non-volatile / high boiling point.

marking_points.point: Non-volatile / high boiling point (printed key also lists oxidising agent)
